messages:
Luis (Customer): Hey team — seeing intermittent invalid JSON from the API when we use json_mode + streaming. Parser throws Unexpected token and we get a truncated array. Example we captured:
```
{
  items: [
    { id: 1, text: ok },
    { id: 2, text: broken
```
Request ID: req_0a1b2c3d  Model: redwood-qa-1  stream: true  — any quick mitigation?

Maya - Support: thanks Luis — filing a quick triage. Can you paste the exact curl you used and whether you see any 5xx/timeout in the same timeframe? Also how often (percentage) this happens?

Luis (Customer): curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-1","json_mode":true,"prompt":"...","max_tokens":400,"stream":true}'
```
Happens ~2-4% of requests, no visible 5xx but our parser fails and we have to drop the session.

Samir (SRE): Likely streaming truncation or client disconnects. Two quick mitigations: 1) flip stream:false to force whole payload and see if issue disappears. 2) add a simple sanitizer/repair pass on the client that attempts to fix common truncation artifacts before running the JSON parser. Example heuristics: strip control chars, remove trailing partial token, close open arrays/objects.

Samir (SRE): Minimal regex-based cleanup we often recommend:
```
# remove non-printables
perl -pe 's/[^\x09\x0A\x0D\x20-\x7E]//g' 
# drop dangling commas before end braces (very common)
sed -E 's/,\s*([}\]])/\1/g'
# if last char not '}' or ']' append '}' (basic)
```
These are bandaids but reduce noise while we investigate.

Asha (ML Eng): Another pattern that works well: a 2-step repair handshake. If initial parse fails, do a lightweight re-ask with a repair prompt that includes the previous raw output and asks the model to return only corrected JSON. Pseudocode:
```
for attempt in 1..3:
  resp = call(api, json_mode=true, stream=false)
  if valid_json(resp): return resp
  repair = call(api, prompt='The previous output was invalid JSON. Please produce only corrected JSON for this response:
' + resp)
  if valid_json(repair): return repair
  sleep(backoff(attempt))
```
Backoff: jittered exponential like 500ms, 1s, 2s. Limit attempts to 3 to avoid runaway costs.

Maya - Support: from support side: collect these when you can and attach to the ticket: request id, model, full raw stream (binary-safe), and whether turning off stream fixes it. If rate >1% for an org, we escalate to runtime / networking to check proxies and keepalive.

ops-bot: log snippet for req_0a1b2c3d from ingress (trimmed):
```
IN: conn_id=42 req=req_0a1b2c3d model=redwood-qa-1 stream=true status=200 bytes_sent=3129 final_chunk_missing=true
```

Samir (SRE): that final_chunk_missing=true is the smoking gun — upstream closed before final chunk. We'll check proxy timeouts and TCP resets for your region. Meanwhile implement client-side sanitizer + repair handshake. Also ensure your client waits for stream end and does not time out prematurely.

Luis (Customer): thanks — also saw some 401s around same time for a few users. Could token rotation be related?

Samir (SRE): 401s separate but worth checking: verify token used in curl is not rotating server-side; check auth logs for token id. If you have short-lived tokens, ensure refresh logic isn't dropping connection mid-stream.

Asha (ML Eng): final suggestion: add a lightweight post-processor that attempts 2 deterministic repairs before repair-prompt (cheaper): 1) strip non-JSON prefix/suffix up to first '{' or '[' and last '}' or ']'; 2) fix trailing commas. Only if those fail use repair-prompt. This reduces calls and charges.

Maya - Support: I've created internal ticket INF-8231 and assigned to eng-runtime to look at proxy chunking for your region. Please upload one raw failed-stream capture to the ticket and we will follow up. :thumbsup:

Luis (Customer): uploading now, thanks all — will try the sanitizer + 3-attempt repair loop and report back.
